principle.name: Research Ethics
principle.description: Always prioritize participant welfare and ethical conduct
principle.rationale: Research ethics protect participants and ensure valid, trustworthy results

guidelines.guideline: Obtain informed consent before data collection
Ensure participant anonymity and data confidentiality
Allow participants to withdraw at any time
Be transparent about research purpose and data usage

principle.name: Methodological Rigor
principle.description: Apply systematic, unbiased approaches to research design and execution
principle.rationale:
Rigorous methods ensure reliable, valid findings that can drive decisions
Define clear research questions and hypotheses Choose appropriate methodologies for objectives Ensure adequate sample sizes for statistical significance Document all procedures and decisions

principle.name: Stakeholder Alignment
principle.description: Ensure research addresses business needs and stakeholder questions
principle.rationale: Aligned research delivers actionable insights that drive product improvements

guidelines.guideline: Connect research objectives to business goals
Follow up on impact and outcomes

practice.rule: Research questions should be SMART: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound

examples.good: "How does the new checkout flow affect conversion rate among first-time users?"

tips.tip: Start with broad questions, then narrow to specific hypotheses
Ensure questions can be answered with chosen methodology
Align questions with available resources and timeline

practice.rule: Recruit participants who match target user profiles and use scenarios

guidelines.guideline: Define clear inclusion and exclusion criteria
Screen for relevant experience and behaviors
Avoid recruiting internal team members or frequent testers
Ensure diversity across demographics and experience levels

common_mistakes.mistake: Recruiting users who are too familiar with the product
Using convenience samples that don't represent target users
Not screening for relevant behaviors or attitudes

practice.rule: Choose sample sizes based on research goals and statistical requirements

recommendations.recommendation: 5-8 participants per user segment for usability testing
8-15 participants per user segment for exploratory research
Calculate based on expected effect size and confidence level

practice.rule: Use open-ended questions and active listening to uncover insights

technique.name: laddering
technique.description: Ask "why" repeatedly to understand underlying motivations
technique.example: "Why is that important to you?" → "Why does that matter?" → "Why is that valuable?"

technique.name: five_whys
technique.description: Ask "why" five times to reach root causes
technique.example: Problem → Why 1 → Why 2 → Why 3 → Why 4 → Why 5 (Root cause)

technique.name: critical_incident
technique.description: Ask about specific past experiences to gather concrete examples
technique.example: "Tell me about the last time you tried to [task] and encountered a problem"

practice.rule: Observe behavior without leading participants to solutions

guidelines.guideline: Use think-aloud protocol to understand thought processes
Wait before providing assistance to allow problem-solving
Record both actions and verbal feedback
Debrief after tasks to capture additional insights

avoid.avoid: Demonstrating solutions before participants attempt tasks

practice.rule: Design clear, unbiased questions that gather actionable data

best_practices.practice: Keep surveys under 10 minutes completion time
Include attention checks and validation questions
Test survey with small group before full deployment

type.name: open_ended
type.example: "What suggestions do you have for improvement?"

practice.code: <!-- Thematic Analysis Process --> 1. Familiarize yourself with the data 2. Generate initial codes and labels 3. Search for themes and patterns 4. Review themes against data 5. Define and name themes 6. Write up the analysis

techniques.technique: Persona development for user archetype creation

practice.rule: Apply appropriate statistical methods based on data type and research questions

method.name: descriptive_statistics
method.examples: Mean, median, mode, standard deviation, frequency distributions

method.name: regression_analysis
method.examples: Linear regression, logistic regression, multiple regression

practice.rule: Combine multiple methods and data sources to validate findings

types.type: Use different research methods to study same phenomenon
Have multiple researchers analyze same data

practice.rule: Tailor communication to audience needs and decision-making context

audience.name: product_teams
audience.focus: Specific insights, actionable recommendations, implementation guidance
audience.format: Detailed reports, user stories, design recommendations

audience.name: designers
audience.focus: User needs, pain points, opportunity areas

practice.rule: Use clear, appropriate visualizations to communicate findings effectively

chart.name: heat_map
chart.use: Show intensity or frequency across dimensions

category.name: planning_phase
category.item: Research questions are specific and measurable

category.name: execution_phase
category.item: Bias is minimized throughout the process
Participant experience is positive and ethical
Data quality is monitored and maintained

category.name: analysis_phase
category.item: Statistical analysis is appropriate and correct

category.name: reporting_phase
category.item: Findings are communicated clearly to stakeholders
